name: Baanah
bio: Baanah was the son of Rimmon the Beerothite, a Benjamite, brother of Rechab, and an officer under Ish-Bosheth. After Abner's death left Ish-Bosheth disheartened, Baanah and Rechab slipped into his house while he lay resting at noon, pretending to fetch wheat, and struck him down in his bed, then cut off his head and brought it to David at Hebron by night, expecting a rich reward and declaring, "The LORD has avenged my lord the king today on Saul and his offspring" (2 Samuel 4:1-8). David instead sharply rebuked them, recalling how he had put to death the Amalekite who merely claimed to have killed Saul, and ordered Rechab and Baanah executed, their hands and feet cut off and their bodies hung by the pool at Hebron (2 Samuel 4:9-12). Baanah's expected reward instead cost him his life, for murdering a descendant of "the LORD's anointed" — a fate identical to that of the Amalekite who had made a similar miscalculation.
